topic: 7 borders that make no sense, ending on India's Tin Bigha Corridor
hook: Your map of India hides a tiny road that Bangladesh is allowed to use, and it is the strangest border on Earth.
title: 7 Borders That Make No Sense (India's Is Craziest)
description:
Seven real borders that look like mistakes on the map, counting down from a split Brunei to a gate on an Indian road. Every place is real and checkable on any map. Watch to the end for India's strangest border of all, the Tin Bigha Corridor.

#borders #geography #india
comment_prompt: Which border was the strangest for you?

chapters.title: The Gambia: a country in a river

scenes.narration: Your map of India hides a tiny road that Bangladesh is allowed to use, and it is the strangest border on Earth.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest Border

scenes.narration: Seven real borders are coming, counting down, and every one of them looks like a mistake someone made on the map.
scenes.headline: Seven Real Borders

scenes.narration: By the end, you'll see a gate on an Indian road that lets another country's citizens walk straight through.
scenes.headline: A Gate On An Indian Road

scenes.narration: Each border is stranger than the one before it, so stay for the whole list if you want to see India's.
scenes.headline: Each One Stranger

scenes.narration: But first, a country that is cut into two pieces, so you cannot drive across it without leaving it.
scenes.headline: A Country In Two Pieces

scenes.narration: Number seven: Brunei, a small, rich country on the island of Borneo, shaped like two pieces that do not touch.
scenes.headline: Brunei Split In Two

scenes.narration: A strip of Malaysia called Limbang runs all the way to the sea and splits Brunei into a western part and an eastern part.
scenes.headline: Limbang Cuts Through

scenes.narration: That strip is part of the Malaysian state of Sarawak, which means Malaysia sits right in the middle of Brunei.
scenes.headline: Malaysia In The Middle

scenes.narration: For years, driving from one half to the other meant leaving Brunei, entering Malaysia, and then entering Brunei again.
scenes.headline: Leave And Re-Enter

scenes.narration: That meant passports, stamps and queues, just to travel between two parts of the very same country.
scenes.headline: Stamps To Cross Home

scenes.narration: Since 2020, a long bridge lets drivers skip Malaysia, but the map still shows Brunei in two separate pieces.
scenes.headline: A Bridge Since 2020

scenes.narration: That is a split country. The next one is a whole country squeezed into the shape of a river.
scenes.headline: A Country Shaped Like A River

scenes.narration: Number six: The Gambia, in West Africa, a country that looks like a finger poked into the middle of another one.
scenes.headline: The Gambia

scenes.narration: It follows the Gambia River inland, and it is only about 25 to 50 kilometres wide.
scenes.headline: A Thin Strip

scenes.narration: Senegal surrounds it on every side except the short Atlantic coast, so the whole country is basically one river valley.
scenes.headline: Surrounded By Senegal

scenes.narration: Both banks of the river are Gambian, which makes that one river the heart of the entire country.
scenes.headline: A River Is The Country

scenes.narration: Britain and France shaped these lines in colonial times, and the strange outline survived long after both left.
scenes.headline: Colonial Lines

scenes.narration: Imagine a whole country wrapped by its only land neighbour, like a thread running through the middle of a bigger one.
scenes.headline: A Thread In Senegal

scenes.narration: Strange, yes. But the next countries have a bigger problem: pieces of them are cut off, far away from home.
scenes.headline: Cut-Off Pieces Next

scenes.narration: Number five: Nakhchivan, a part of Azerbaijan that is completely cut off from the rest of the country.
scenes.headline: Nakhchivan

scenes.narration: Armenia lies in between, so mainland Azerbaijan and Nakhchivan do not share a single metre of border.
scenes.headline: Armenia In Between

scenes.narration: It touches Iran, Turkey and Armenia, but not the country it belongs to, which is a very odd way to be part of a nation.
scenes.headline: Touches Everyone But Home

scenes.narration: Nakhchivan is an autonomous republic inside Azerbaijan, with its own parliament, yet it sits on the far side of another country.
scenes.headline: Its Own Parliament

scenes.narration: To reach the rest of Azerbaijan, people usually fly or take a long route around through other countries.
scenes.headline: Fly Or Go Around

scenes.narration: Number four: Cabinda, an oil-rich piece of Angola on the Atlantic coast, and it is not connected to Angola.
scenes.headline: Cabinda

scenes.narration: A narrow strip of the Democratic Republic of the Congo reaches the sea and cuts Cabinda completely off.
scenes.headline: Congo's Strip

scenes.narration: Put one finger on Angola and another on Cabinda, and you will find Congo's strip sitting between your fingers.
scenes.headline: A Gap On The Map

scenes.narration: So Angola owns a province you cannot reach by road without first crossing into another country.
scenes.headline: No Road Home

scenes.narration: That strip of Congo exists because of old colonial deals, not because anyone planned a sensible map.
scenes.headline: Old Deals, Odd Map

scenes.narration: Stay with me, because number three is cut off on an island, with another country all around it.
scenes.headline: Cut Off On An Island

scenes.narration: Number three: Oecusse, a pocket of East Timor sitting inside Indonesian West Timor, with the sea on its other side.
scenes.headline: Oecusse

scenes.narration: The main part of East Timor is far away on the same island, and Indonesia lies in between.
scenes.headline: Indonesia In Between

scenes.narration: It is a small patch of land on the northern coast, hemmed in by Indonesian territory and the sea.
scenes.headline: A Patch By The Sea

scenes.narration: To go from one part of East Timor to the other, you cross Indonesian land or you take a boat.
scenes.headline: Cross Land Or Sail

scenes.narration: Portugal ruled this pocket for centuries while the Dutch ruled the west, and the odd shape is a leftover from that.
scenes.headline: A Portuguese Leftover

scenes.narration: Three cut-off pieces so far. The last two are on our side of the world, and one is inside India.
scenes.headline: Now Inside India

scenes.narration: If you like strange places and facts like these, subscribe, because we post more things that sound fake but are true.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: Number two: Dahagram and Angarpota, Bangladeshi villages in West Bengal, surrounded on all sides by Indian land.
scenes.headline: Dahagram-Angarpota

scenes.narration: Take a few steps in any direction from these villages, and you are standing in India, not in Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: One Step To India

scenes.narration: They sit in the Cooch Behar area, near the border in northern West Bengal, with Indian farms on every side.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar Area

scenes.narration: For decades their biggest problem was simple: the way to the rest of Bangladesh ran across Indian land.
scenes.headline: A Road Problem

scenes.narration: Villagers needed a way out of their own country's pocket, and that need created the strangest border of all.
scenes.headline: A Way Out Needed

scenes.narration: Remember Dahagram, because number one is the road that solves it, and you can find it on a map of India.
scenes.headline: Number One Is Next

scenes.narration: Number one: the Tin Bigha Corridor, a small strip of Indian land leased to Bangladesh so its citizens can reach Dahagram.
scenes.headline: Tin Bigha Corridor

scenes.narration: The name is plain: tin means three in Bengali, and bigha is an old unit of land used in India.
scenes.headline: Three Bigha Of Land

scenes.narration: It connects the villages to the Bangladeshi mainland, so people can walk or ride from their homes to their own country.
scenes.headline: A Path To Bangladesh

scenes.narration: The land under that road is still Indian, but another country's citizens are allowed to use it.
scenes.headline: Indian Land, Foreign Users

scenes.narration: The lease was agreed in 1992, and it turned a locked-in village into a place with a way out.
scenes.headline: Leased In 1992

scenes.narration: And along the strip stands a gate that has opened and closed at set hours, like a shop with a timetable.
scenes.headline: A Gate With Hours

scenes.narration: When the gate was shut, the villages were locked inside India again, and no one could simply walk out.
scenes.headline: Shut Means Stuck

scenes.narration: Border guards watch the strip, so people move along it under watchful eyes, on a path that two countries care about.
scenes.headline: Guards Watch The Strip

scenes.narration: For people living there, the corridor is the difference between being trapped and being able to reach the rest of their country.
scenes.headline: Trapped Or Free

scenes.narration: Indian land, a Bangladeshi route and a gate on a timetable. That is why this border is number one.
scenes.headline: Number One Border

scenes.narration: So go back to the start: a tiny road on India's map that Bangladesh is allowed to use. Now you know where it is.
scenes.headline: That Tiny Road

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: more places on the map that look fake but are completely real. See you there.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow: More Real Maps
